{{Indian name|Gopinath|Gorur Ramaswamy Iyengar}}[[Captain (armed forces)|Captain]] '''Gorur Ramaswamy Iyengar Gopinath''' (born 13 November 1951)<ref>{{Cite web|title=GR Gopinath: Latest News & Videos, Photos about GR Gopinath {{!}} The Economic Times|url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/topic/gr-gopinath|access-date=2020-11-12|website=The Economic Times}}</ref><ref>{{Citation|title=The Unstoppable Indians: Capt. G R Gopinath, founder, Air Deccan (Aired: March 2009)| date=16 January 2014 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yw12bEPWpsc |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/varchive/youtube/20211219/yw12bEPWpsc |archive-date=2021-12-19 |url-status=live|access-date=2020-01-20}}{{cbignore}}</ref> is an Indian entrepreneur,<ref>{{cite web |url=http://mybtechlife.com/the-list-of-great-entrepreneurs-in-india-2015/ |title=The List of Great Entrepreneurs of India in 2015 |publisher=MyBTechLife |author=Srikar Muthyala |date=29 September 2015 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160114000446/http://mybtechlife.com/the-list-of-great-entrepreneurs-in-india-2015/ |archive-date=2016-01-14 }}</ref> the founder of [[Simplifly Deccan]], a retired Captain of the [[Indian Army]], an author and a politician.<ref name=gulf/><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.theweekendleader.com/Success/221/he-hops-on,-simply.html|access-date=1 May 2012|date=1 May 2012|publisher=The Weekend Leader|last=Bengaluru|first=Sudha Narasimhachar|title=Adored by millions, Capt Gopinath is a man of many faces}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|publisher=Matpal.com|url=http://www.matpal.com/2012/02/captain-gr-gopinath-founder-of-air.html|access-date=1 May 2012|date=8 February 2012|title=Captain G R Gopinath: Founder of Air Deccan|archive-date=27 April 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130427004450/http://www.matpal.com/2012/02/captain-gr-gopinath-founder-of-air.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>

== Early life ==
Gopinath was born in [[Gorur, Hassan]], in a [[Tamils|Tamil]] [[Iyengar]] family and was brought up in a small village in Gorur in the [[Hassan district]] of [[Karnataka State]]. Gopinath's father Gorur Ramaswamy Iyengar, a school teacher (not to be confused with Kannada Novelist [[Gorur Ramaswamy Iyengar]] who is his mother's uncle), believed that schools were systems of regimentation and was resolved to teach Gopinath at home.<ref name=gulf/>

However, Gopinath was admitted to a [[Kannada]] medium school quite late and straight away he joined Standard V. Gopinath didn't clear the military school entrance on the first attempt because he wasn't fluent in English. After his headmaster wrote to the defence ministry, Gopinath was allowed to write the exam in Kannada and he cleared the entrance on his second attempt.<ref name="Forbes">{{cite journal |title=G. R. Gopinath: Jonathan Livingston Seagull |journal=Forbes India |url=https://www.forbesindia.com/article/zen-garden/g-r-gopinath-jonathan-livingston-seagull/12882/1 |access-date=12 July 2024 |language=en}}</ref> 

In 1962, after Gopinath cleared the admission test, he joined [[Sainik School, Bijapur]]. The school helped and prepared Gopinath to clear the [[National Defence Academy|NDA]] entrance exams. After 3 years of vigorous training, Gopinath completed education from the National Defence Academy, Pune. He then went on to graduate from the [[Indian Military Academy|Indian Military Academy, Dehradun]].<ref name=gulf/>

==Career==
After school, he earned a commission in the [[Indian Army]]. When he was graduating in 1971, his training was cut short when the 1971 [[Bangladesh Liberation War]] broke out. He was 20 when he was first posted to [[Sikkim]]. He later rose to the rank of [[Army ranks and insignia of India|Captain]]. But he was not happy with waiting for a promotion in the army.<ref>{{cite web |title=G. R. Gopinath: Jonathan Livingston Seagull |url=https://www.forbesindia.com/article/zen-garden/g-r-gopinath-jonathan-livingston-seagull/12882/1 |website=Forbes India |access-date=12 July 2024 |language=en}}</ref> 

He took early retirement from Indian Army, at the age of 28. Upon retirement from the armed forces, he established an ecologically sustainable [[sericulture]] farm; his innovative methods earned him the [[Rolex Awards for Enterprise|Rolex Laureate Award]] in 1996.<ref name=gulf/> Next, he started the Malnad Mobikes (Enfield dealership) and opened a hotel in Hassan.<ref>{{Cite book |isbn = 978-93-5029-155-9|title = Simply Fly : A Deccan Odyssey|date = 9 May 2011| publisher=HarperCollins Publishers India }}</ref>

In 1997 he co-founded Deccan Aviation, a charter helicopter service with his two friends, who were also in air force. In 2003, Gopinath founded [[Simplifly Deccan|Air Deccan]], a low cost airline; Air Deccan merged with Kingfisher Airlines in 2007. In 2009 he founded [[Deccan 360]], a freight flight business. In July 2013, [[Deccan 360]] was ordered to wind up by the [[Karnataka High Court]] order based on petitions filed by Dubai-based United Aviation Services (UAS) and another by M/s Patel Integrated Logistics (PIL) Pvt. Ltd. – seeking recovery of amounts due to them by winding up the company.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.thehindu.com/news/national/karnataka/its-curtains-for-deccan-360/article4912777.ece |title=It's curtains for Deccan 360 |newspaper=The Hindu |date=2013-07-14 |access-date=2016-01-07}}</ref>

In May 2006, he was knighted with "[[Legion of Honour|Chevalier de la Legion d’Honneur]]" the civilian award conferred by the French Government. He has received many awards for Air Deccan.<ref name=gulf/>

In 2009, Gopinath contested as an independent candidate in Bangalore South constituency at the Lok Sabha elections but was defeated.

In 2014, he unsuccessfully contested Lok Sabha elections on the ticket of the [[Aam Aadmi Party]].<ref>{{cite web|author=ET Bureau|url=http://articles.economictimes.indiatimes.com/2009-03-27/news/28459242_1_ls-seat-captain-gopinath-budget-carrier |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140202215107/http://articles.economictimes.indiatimes.com/2009-03-27/news/28459242_1_ls-seat-captain-gopinath-budget-carrier |url-status=dead |archive-date=2 February 2014 |title=Captain Gopinath to fight LS elections – timesofindia-economictimes |work=The Economic Times |access-date=2016-01-07}}</ref> He quit the party citing difference with [[Arvind Kejriwal]] for lack of internal democracy within the party.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Iyer |first=Lakshmi |last2= |last3= |first3= |title=Gopinath quits AAP; cite lack of democracy, ‘scoot and shoot politics’ |url=https://bangaloremirror.indiatimes.com/news/india/captain-gopinath-bangalore-aapm-quits-aap-shazia-imly-aam-aadmi-party-loss-lok-sabha-arvind-kejriwal/articleshow/35569180.cms |access-date=2025-02-01 |website=Bangalore Mirror |language=en}}</ref>

== Aviation career ==

=== Deccan Aviation ===
Gopinath moved to Bengaluru in 1992 where he bumped into Captain K.J. Samuel, who was his friend in the army. Samuel was a freelance pilot and was planning to set-up a commercial Helicopter service. In 1995, when the Indian government started a regulatory reforms process to encourage entrepreneurship, Gopinath partnered with Samuel and established Deccan Aviation.<ref name=gulf/>
Deccan's helicopters were chartered by most politicians and the company also got involved in many rescue missions in Sri Lanka, Nepal, Kabul and South India.
The Company grew to become one of the largest private air charter companies in India and Sri Lanka.<ref>{{Cite book|title = New Age Marketing: Emerging Realities|last = Dhar|first = Upinder|publisher = Excel Books|year = 2008|location = New Delhi|page = 71}}</ref>

Inspired by the success of [[Southwest Airlines]] in the United States and [[Ryanair]] in Europe, Deccan Aviation launched India's first low-cost airline, [[Simplifly Deccan|Air Deccan]] in 2003.<ref>{{cite news|title=Air Deccan plans 'very low-cost' flights |url=http://www.rediff.com/money/2003/jul/02spec1.htm |work=[[Rediff.com]] |date= 2 July 2003 |access-date=18 December 2017}}</ref>
Deccan Aviation went public in May 2006,<ref name= HBL>{{cite news|title=Deccan Aviation IPO on 18 May, price band Rs. 150-175 |url=http://www.thehindubusinessline.com/todays-paper/tp-markets/deccan-aviation-ipo-on-may-18-price-band-rs-150175/article1733555.ece |newspaper=[[Business Line]]|location=Chennai |date= 12 May 2006 |access-date=18 December 2017}}</ref> however by then the airline was losing money.<ref name= LMT>{{cite news|title=Speculation in the air as Deccan Aviation scrambles for new cash |url=http://www.livemint.com/Companies/cZNvBEb4dniT28nsdCkWnN/Speculation-in-the-air-as-Deccan-Aviation-scrambles-for-new.html |publisher=[[Live Mint]] |date= 19 May 2007 |access-date=18 December 2017}}</ref> The following year, the [[Vijay Mallya]] lead UB group purchased a strategic 26 per cent stake in Deccan Aviation.<ref name= HBL2>{{cite news|title=Vijay Mallya lands 26% stake in Deccan Aviation |url=http://www.thehindubusinessline.com/todays-paper/vijay-mallya-lands-26-stake-in-deccan-aviation/article1659803.ece |newspaper=[[Business Line]]|location=Chennai |date= 1 June 2007 |access-date=18 December 2017}}</ref>
At the time of purchase, Air Deccan connected sixty nine cities around India.<ref name=gulf>{{cite web|publisher=Gulf News|access-date=1 May 2012|title=Adopting a revolutionary approach|date=8 April 2011|last=Pathak|first=Nilima|url=http://gulfnews.com/life-style/people/adopting-a-revolutionary-approach-1.786853}}</ref>
Mallya merged the two airlines soon after<ref name= HBL3>{{cite news|title=Kingfisher Airlines, Deccan decide to merge |url=http://www.thehindubusinessline.com/todays-paper/kingfisher-airlines-deccan-decide-to-merge/article1677985.ece |newspaper=[[Business Line]]|location=Chennai |date= 20 December 2007 |access-date=18 December 2017}}</ref> and Capt. Gopinath sold most of his stake in the company in 2009.<ref name= LM2>{{cite news|title=Gopinath reduces stake in Kingfisher to 1.75% |url=http://www.livemint.com/Companies/t3pa48Rd4JxzW1lI66AHML/Gopinath-reduces-stake-in-Kingfisher-to-175.html |publisher=[[Live Mint]] |date= 17 September 2009 |access-date=18 December 2017}}</ref>

=== Deccan Charters ===
During the merger process of Kingfisher with Air Deccan, the Charter services division of Deccan Aviation was transferred into a new company named [[Deccan Charters]] Limited after it received its Non-Scheduled Air Operator Permit (NSOP) from the DGCA on 10 October 2008. During that period, the Charter operations continued to perform satisfactorily and increased its presence in off shore flying for the oil sector.<ref>{{cite web|title = Director Report Kingfisher Airlines Ltd. |url = https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/directorsreport.cms?companyid=276&year=2008 | website = ET Markets.com |access-date = 19 December 2017}}</ref>

Gopinath used the money from the UB Group deal to start [[Deccan 360]], a cargo airline, in May 2009. But that enterprise too was squeezed by a severe cash crunch and shut shop in 2011. The same year, Gopinath became the 100% owner of Deccan Charters by purchasing the stake Mallya held in the company as part of the 2007 deal.<ref name= ET1>{{cite news|title=GR Gopinath's Deccan Charters faces severe crisis; puts entire fleet of aircraft on sale |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/transportation/airlines-/-aviation/gr-gopinaths-deccan-charters-faces-severe-crisis-puts-entire-fleet-of-aircraft-on-sale/articleshow/17620998.cms |work=[[The Economic Times]] |date= 15 December 2012 |access-date=19 December 2017}}</ref>
The following year, Gopinath launched daily charter flights in the state of Gujarat under the brand name of Deccan Shuttles. The flights connected Ahmedabad, Surat, Jamnagar, Bhavnagar and Kandla using a nine-seater Cessna Grand Caravan aircraft.<ref name= LM1>{{cite news|title=Deccan Shuttles to launch operations in Gujarat on Monday |url=http://www.livemint.com/Companies/HctiI7me9Xgp7Le5qCyfiM/Deccan-Shuttles-to-launch-operations-in-Gujarat-on-Monday.html |publisher=[[Live Mint]] |date= 18 August 2012 |access-date=19 December 2017}}</ref> The service wound up in 2013.

In April 2017, Deccan charters bid for and won 34 regional Indian routes under the UDAN scheme.<ref name= BS>{{cite news|title=Captain Gopinath back in the game; Deccan Charter to fly on regional routes |url=http://www.business-standard.com/article/companies/captain-gopinath-back-in-the-game-deccan-charter-to-fly-on-regional-routes-117032700106_1.html|work=[[Business Standard]] |date= 27 March 2017 |access-date=19 December 2017}}</ref> Operating under the brand name [[Air Deccan]], it commenced operations in December 2017. Air Deccan operated 19-seater [[Beechcraft 1900D]] turboprop aircraft that are suitable for short-haul flights. The airline has planned to connect Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata and Shillong to regional towns in the vicinity of these cities.<ref name= BT>{{cite news|title=Aviation pioneer GR Gopinath makes comeback with Air Deccan, to start disruptive Re 1 tickets |url=http://www.businesstoday.in/sectors/aviation/gr-gopinath-air-deccan-re-1-tickets-low-cost-airlines-cheap-flights/story/266075.html |publisher=[[Business Today (India)]] |date= 15 December 2017 |access-date=19 December 2017}}</ref> However, it could not operate a large number of the RCS routes awarded to it due to the company's weak financials. Scheduled commercial operations were stopped in April 2020 due to the effects of the [[COVID-19 pandemic]] and the ensuing lockdown.<ref>{{cite news|title=Air Deccan ceases its operations, all employees put on sabbatical. |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/business/india-business/air-deccan-ceases-its-operations-all-employees-put-on-sabbatical-without-pay/articleshow/74994496.cms|publisher=[[Times of India]] |date= 5 April 2020 |access-date=11 August 2025}}</ref>

== In popular culture ==

The 2020 Indian Tamil-language film ''[[Soorarai Pottru]]'' (or Udaan, in Hindi) was partly inspired by events from the life of Gopinath and is based on his memoir ''Simply Fly: A Deccan Odyssey''.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Sudha Kongara invested 10 years for Soorarai Pottru: Suriya |url=https://www.sify.com/movies/sudha-kongara-invested-10-years-for-soorarai-pottru-suriya--news-tamil-ucoeivhaajcdd.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210625072821/https://www.sify.com/movies/sudha-kongara-invested-10-years-for-soorarai-pottru-suriya--news-tamil-ucoeivhaajcdd.html |archive-date=25 June 2021 |access-date=25 June 2021 |website=[[Sify]]}}</ref>

In 2024, ''[[Soorarai Pottru]]'' is remade in Hindi as ''[[Sarfira]]'' starring [[Akshay Kumar]] and released.

extract: Captain Gorur Ramaswamy Iyengar Gopinath (born 13 November 1951) is an Indian entrepreneur, the founder of Simplifly Deccan, a retired Captain of the Indian Army, an author and a politician.
